intervals.label: construction
intervals.note: J-PARC facility construction started December 2001; the main ring reached its initial design energy in December 2008.
intervals.quote: December  Construction of J-PARC facilities started.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.quote: December  Initial target energy (30 GeV) was achieved at MR.

intervals.label: shutdown after the Great East Japan Earthquake
intervals.note: The October 2011 T2K status report states the beam stopped on 11 March 2011 and that J-PARC was "on schedule to resume operations ... in December 2011"; no source read on 2026-09-16 confirms the actual restart date, so the end is recorded as the planned date.
intervals.quote: The T2K data taking stopped abruptly on March 11 2011 due to the Great East Japan Earthquake.

intervals.label: operation at 760 kW after the 2023 beamline upgrade
intervals.note: Beam power reached about 710 kW in stable operation and a record 760 kW on 25 December 2023.

beam_energy.note: Kinetic energy. The J-PARC MR page still describes the machine as a "50 GeV (currently 30 GeV) main ring"; 30 GeV is the energy actually used for the neutrino beam.
beam_energy.quote: Circumference 1567 m Beam power ~750 kW Beam kinetic energy 30 GeV

beam_power.note: Beam power history: ~145 kW by March 2011 (T2K Run 1-2); design ~750 kW in the T2K instrumentation paper; about 710 kW in stable operation and a record 760 kW on 25 December 2023; the upgrade programme aims at 1.3 MW.

circumference.note: The J-PARC accelerators page rounds this to "about 1600 m".

summary.plain: The largest J-PARC accelerator: a 1.6-kilometre ring that accelerates protons to 30 billion electronvolts and fires them at the target that makes the neutrino beam.
summary.technical: 30 GeV fast-extraction proton synchrotron, 1567 m circumference, design beam power ~750 kW, 760 kW reached in December 2023, with an upgrade programme towards 1.3 MW for Hyper-Kamiokande.
